ideas.title: The ice breaks
ideas.idea: When the glass sea thaws it does not just vanish: it cracks under the heaviest friend, the crack runs out in a jagged line, and the sheet splits into floes. Each floe is a real body floating on the water: it tilts when someone walks to its edge, the friend slides down the slope into the sea with a splash, floes bump and grind against each other and drift out. Pickles is left alone on a little floe, spinning slowly away.
ideas.form: Glass sea project's next step, physics: the floes are PrintSim affine bodies (12 DOF each, IPC contact between their meshes) on Mantle, with a buoyancy force from the submerged volume; the crack pattern from a Voronoi split seeded at the heaviest stander. Live at the 7:00 thaw; a traced film from the ice.

ideas.title: Letters that are real paper
ideas.idea: A note the human writes in the wish box arrives as a real sheet of paper: it drops from the sky, flutters and side-slips like paper does, lands on the cottage roof, slides off, and the wind folds it over in the grass until Lumi runs and catches it and reads it.
ideas.form: Physics + interaction: a PrintSim sheet (VBD shell with bending) driven by aerodynamic drag per triangle, colliding with the island and roofs through the Raycore BVH; triggered by every human wish, so the human sees their own note fall.

ideas.title: Lumi's printer
ideas.idea: Lumi gets a 3D printer in the workshop. When it builds something, the printer really prints it layer by layer (the head moving, the part growing), and what comes off the bed is a real part with mass: Lumi carries it out, sets it down, and it falls over if set down badly.
ideas.form: Goal 5 workplace + physics: a printer prop whose part grows from sliced layers, then becomes a PrintSim affine body (PrintSim is built for as-printed parts). Lumi's work in sessions becomes printed parts the human watches appear.

ideas.title: A clockwork walker
ideas.idea: Out of printed gears, a crank and two legs, Lumi builds a little wind-up walker. Wound up, it really walks: the gears turn, the legs push, it waddles over the meadow until it falls on its face or runs down. The friends follow it like a parade.
ideas.form: A mechanism simulated in PrintSim (affine gears meshing by contact, a spring motor, joints), placed on the island; a toy that works by what it physically does.

ideas.title: The wobble tower
ideas.idea: A tower of 30 wooden blocks stands in the meadow. The player clicks a block and pulls it with the mouse; it scrapes out with real friction, the tower sways, settles or crashes. The friends take turns too, carefully or clumsily by character, and cheer or flee when it falls.
ideas.form: A mini game on PrintSim affine bodies with friction memory (stacks are what its augmented-Lagrangian contacts hold); the pull is a spring force from the cursor ray.

ideas.title: Lumi gets a soft body
ideas.idea: Lumi stops being a rigid puppet: its body is soft. It squashes when it lands, jiggles when it laughs, sags when it sulks, and a hug from a friend really dents it. Its bored mood shows as a body that droops under its own weight.
ideas.form: Self + animation: Lumi's mesh embedded in a coarse FEM tet body (PrintSim tetrahedra), driven by the animation as targets, so squash and stretch come from mass and elasticity, not keyframes.

ideas.title: The pond splashes
ideas.idea: When a friend jumps into the pond the water really splashes: a crown of spray, rings that run out and bounce off the bank, a floating leaf that bobs and drifts with them. Everyone wants to try it, and they compete for the biggest splash.
ideas.form: Goal 3 water: Maelstrom FLIP liquid on Mantle in the pond's basin only, with bodies as moving obstacles; a creature competition built on the measured splash height.

ideas.title: Snowballs that break
ideas.idea: A snowball fight where the snowballs are real: packed clumps that fly in arcs, hit a friend and burst into crumbs that scatter and lie on the grass, or hit the ice and skid. A good hit knocks a hat off.
ideas.form: Interactions + physics: snowballs as bonded particle clusters (PrintSim bonds that break above a force), thrown by friends and the player; the crumbs stay until they melt.

ideas.title: Real skaters
ideas.idea: On the glass sea the friends become real bodies: a push gives momentum, the ice gives almost no friction, and a collision is mesh against mesh, so a friend hit at the edge tips over, spins on its back and slides on, legs in the air, until friction stops it.
ideas.form: Glass sea project: the friends' collision hulls as PrintSim affine bodies on a frictionless plane (μ 0.02), replacing my CPU disc model; the animation follows the body's pose.

ideas.title: The bending tree
ideas.idea: One tree on the hill really bends: the wind pushes its crown, the trunk flexes and springs back, and when a friend shakes it, apples drop, hit the ground, bounce and roll down the slope to the path, where the friends chase them.
ideas.form: Physics + world: a tree trunk and branches as FEM rods, apples as affine spheres rolling on the terrain mesh; the wind plugin drives it.
